transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-02
Time: 11:00 AM ET
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Olivia Chen (Crestwood Head of Cloud Architecture), Marcus Reyes (CISO), Ellen Park (PM)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on data residency, log retention, HIPAA/financial controls and deciding between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment. Customer heavy on compliance and internal audit needs; interested in Private but evaluating cost/tradeoffs.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro — I'm Maya AE for Redwood, with Liam our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Olivia: Hi all, Olivia here. Marcus and Ellen on. We're mostly looking at how Redwood could host our LLM features while respecting data residency and audit controls.
[00:15] Marcus: Yep we have pretty strict rules — data for EU customers must stay ineu, also some PHI flows so HIPAA questions.
[00:22] Liam: Great, that's exactly the scenarios we've been helping with. Quick note: Redwood has Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem). Each has different controls around networking, logs, and residency.
[00:35] Ellen: Can you clarify what "Hosted" actually means for data at rest? Like if we use Hosted, are logs or payloads stored outside our region?
[00:44] Maya: Hosted by default stores in the region you select, but we do maintain limited operational logs. For EU-only residency we usually recommend Dedicated or Private — Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools within a region and we can contractually restrict backups and telemetry, Private gives you a customer-managed control plane.
[00:58] Marcus: What about SOC 2 and encryption? We need at-rest encryption keys that we control, ideally KMS/HSM.
[01:07] Liam: For Private deployments we support customer KMS integrations and HSM for key custody — that means keys never leave your control. For Dedicated we offer BYOK with KMS cross-account options but there are some differences in key provisioning. We'll send the exact doc.
[01:19] Olivia: And audit logs? Our auditors require immutable audit trail of requests, who accessed models, etc, for seven years in some cases.
[01:28] Maya: We have per-request audit logging and can ship logs to your SIEM (S3, Splunk, or partner endpoints). For Private you can keep logs entirely inside your VPC and control retention. For Hosted we have configurable retention windows but long-term retention typically requires an enterprise add-on.
[01:45] Ellen: How noisy are the logs? I worry about PII in logs — do you have automatic PII redaction?
[01:52] Liam: We offer optional PII masking and configurable log scrubbing before export. It's rule-based and we can show patterns. For sensitive PHI flows most customers route raw traffic through Private so they can apply in-house DLP prior to storage.
[02:06] Marcus: From a compliance perspective, we need to know where model artifacts are stored — KV cache, model weights, checkpoints. Any chance those live outside region?
[02:16] Liam: Model artifacts for Hosted are in the provider region. For Dedicated we pin model versions to your fleet and can keep model caches local. Private obviously keeps everything on your infra — runtime and caches. There is some nuance with prefetching and cold starts but we can set policies to avoid cross-region cache pulls.
[02:32] Maya: Also, a lot of customers mistakenly think Dedicated equals full isolation; it is isolated compute but control plane may still be involved for orchestration unless you choose Private. We can be explicit in the contract.
[02:43] Olivia: That helps. Next — GDPR data subject requests: how do we handle deletions/erasure?
[02:49] Liam: We offer per-customer data purging APIs and retention policies. For Hosted, we keep short-term logs and can purge conversation data on request; for Dedicated/Private you get more control and ability to delete local stores. We can provide timeline SLAs for deletion.
[03:03] Marcus: Encryption in transit is a must — TLS 1.2/1.3 ok? Mutual TLS for private endpoints?
[03:08] Liam: TLS 1.3 supported, and mutual TLS is available for Private deployments, and for Dedicated we can establish VPN/Direct Connect or private endpoints depending on the cloud.
[03:20] Ellen: Are your compliance reports available — SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001?
[03:24] Maya: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO; we'll attach the reports and whitepaper. Also our security page lists controls.
[03:33] Marcus: Any FedRAMP / financial-sector-specific attestations? We need PCI / FFIEC-level controls.
[03:38] Liam: We don't have FedRAMP at the platform level yet. For PCI/FFIEC we provide controls and customer responsibilities map. Many banks pair Private deployment with their own network controls to satisfy those frameworks. We can map our controls to their audit checklists.
[03:52] Olivia: What about data egress and vendor sub-processors — where would customer data be visible to your SREs?
[03:58] Maya: Minimal access. We have role-based access controls; access is logged. For Private deployments you can disable remote access or require jump-hosts. For Dedicated we grant limited access for emergency debugging with audit and on-call approvals.
[04:12] Ellen: Latency tradeoffs — our app needs 300ms 95th percentile. If we go Private, do we lose Redwood optimizations like batching and kernel selection?
[04:21] Liam: No, the runtime is the same; batching/compilation optimizations are part of the runtime and ship with Private. But autoscaling and pooling behaviors depend on your infra sizing. We can help size for your SLA.
[04:33] Olivia: Pricing — high-level comparison Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private please.
[04:37] Maya: Hosted is usage-based, lowest operational lift; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit and lower per-token cost; Private has platform licensing and higher upfront integration but gives full control for compliance. We'll send a pricing sketch.
[04:48] Marcus: One more — logging restrictions: our security policy forbids storing full request payloads that contain account numbers or SSNs. Can Redwood mask or block specific fields?
[04:59] Liam: Yes, masks can be applied at the ingestion layer; you can configure patterns or route through your DLP before it hits storage in Private. For Hosted we can apply tokenization or redaction rules but guarantee needs contractual terms.
[05:13] Ellen: Any references from other banks?
[05:16] Maya: We have a few anonymized case studies and bank references; we'll share permissioned contacts.
[05:21] Olivia: Ok rough timeline — we'd like a security review with procurement, then an SE-run private deployment prototype for one app, then a pilot. Timeline target Q2.
[05:31] Marcus: From compliance side we'll need network diagrams, data flows, SOC2, and attestations.
[05:36] Maya: Understood. We'll circulate collateral and schedule the deep-dive.
[05:40] Ellen: On the technical side — can Liam share details about KMS integration and HSM support?
[05:45] Liam: Yes — we'll produce a topology drawing for KMS, describe encryption-at-rest, and outline HSM integration options. Also note there are nuances around key wrapping for multi-region replication.
[05:58] Maya: Great — wrap up: action items — send SOC/ISO docs, security whitepaper, topology, pricing sketch, and schedule SE deep-dive.
[06:08] Olivia: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[06:10] Marcus: Thanks.

Notes: some transcription artifacts: "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cache"; "SOC 2" as "SOC two"; occasional crosstalk masked.

References shared during call: "Redwood Security Whitepaper (link)"; "Private deployment topology (to follow)"; "Pricing sketch spreadsheet (to follow)"

End of transcript
